# Task Plan: SDC Test Randomization Hardening (数值/地址空间变异加固)

## Goal
Audit all SDC detection tests for insufficient operand-value and address-space variation, identify hardening points, and produce an implementation plan for randomization hardening (value randomization + address-space coverage e.g. large malloc, offset randomization) that improves SDC detection coverage without breaking golden-value reproducibility.

## Next Step
User decision on the P1-P17 plan (approve / adjust priorities). After approval: rebase feat/sve-port-avx53 onto origin/main (d69ce8b2), then implement one patch unit at a time.

## Current Phase
Phase 5 (Delivery — presented 2026-09-20; baseline drift noted: tests/cpu/sve from PR #134-136 extends H9/H14 scope, ipsec datasize knob covers half of H6)

## Phases

### Phase 1: Test Audit (operand/address-space variation census)
- [x] Enumerate all test groups (301 files, ~308 test IDs across 30 dirs)
- [x] For each group: how are operands generated? (constant / fixed pattern / RNG per-thread / RNG per-run)
- [x] For each group: how is memory allocated? (static / stack / fixed malloc / sized malloc; single buffer vs multiple; offset randomization?)
- [x] Classify: which tests use random_input/randbits vs hardcoded constants
- [x] Check memory tests (memory/, cache/) for address-space coverage strategy
- [x] Document in findings.md (per-test table)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, 4 parallel audit agents)

### Phase 2: Framework capability survey
- [x] RNG facilities: random32/64/128, frandom*, memset_random, set_random_bits — per-thread streams, AES engine, -s reproducibility, fracture semantics
- [x] Memory allocation helpers: aligned_alloc_safe, ManagedCodeBuffer (RAII mmap), no THP helper needed (THP=always on host)
- [x] How golden-value comparison constrains randomization: all goldens runtime-computed (no source-hardcoded golden constants) → randomization fully compatible; golden must be same-run same-stream
- [x] Existing knobs: -O test.key=value + get_testspecific_knob_value_* (test_knobs.h); no generic --datasize
- [x] mmap/madvise/THP availability on the host: THP=always, ulimit unlimited, 52GB avail, kernel 6.6, device_info[].cache[] populated-but-unused, sysconf cache size broken (returns 0)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, framework survey agent + host probes)

### Phase 3: Gap analysis & hardening-point identification
- [x] Rank tests by (fixed operands, fixed addresses, small working set) — T0/T1/T2 classification in findings.md
- [x] For each hardening point: which randomization technique applies — H1..H15 table in findings.md
- [x] Identify tests where randomization breaks golden values: none (all goldens runtime-computed); constraint is only golden-recompute cost
- [x] Cross-reference 122-CPU SDC hunt mission context: clean-baseline gate + two-phase validation applies to all hardened/new tests
- **Status:** complete

### Phase 4: Plan formulation
- [x] Design common randomization helpers (if framework-level) vs per-test changes → decided: per-test changes using existing framework RNG + knobs; ONE new test (random_access_sweep); NO new framework surface
- [x] One-patch-per-unit decomposition matching CLAUDE.md patch discipline → P1..P17 units in final plan doc
- [x] Verification strategy per unit (build + run + regression + x86 non-regression + 122 two-phase for new tests)
- [x] Write final plan doc to docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-19-sdc-randomization-hardening.md
- **Status:** complete

### Phase 5: Delivery
- [ ] Present audit table + hardening points + plan to user
- [ ] Get approval / feedback
- **Status:** in_progress

## Decisions Made

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.

- planning-with-files:plan-zht: 啟動 Manus 風格的檔案規劃。為複雜任務建立 task_plan.md、findings.md、progress.md。
- planning-with-files:plan: Start Manus-style file-based planning. Creates task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md for complex tasks.
- planning-with-files:pwf: Short alias for /plan. Starts Manus-style file-based planning: task_plan.md, findings.md, progress.md. Available since v3.0.0.
- planning-with-files:status: Show current planning status at a glance - phases, progress, and any logged errors.
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- planning-with-files:planning-with-files: Persistent file-based planning for multi-step AI-agent work. Keeps task_plan.md, findings.md, and progress.md on disk; lifecycle hooks inject selected project planning context. Automatic recovery reads project planning files only. Explicit session-catchup.py --metadata reads same-project local agent session records and emits aggregate counts only; --replay may emit bounded nonce-framed excerpts. Optional gated mode can request continuation only when the host supports it and never runs commands declared in Markdown. The skill has no network upload path. Use for research or work needing 5+ tool calls.
- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints
- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- sourcegraph:searching-sourcegraph: Use when the user needs to search or navigate code with Sourcegraph MCP tools. Provides disciplined search workflows for finding implementations, understanding systems, debugging issues, fixing bugs, and reviewing code.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

# Task Plan: SDC Test Randomization Hardening (数值/地址空间变异加固)

## Goal
Audit all SDC detection tests for insufficient operand-value and address-space variation, identify hardening points, and produce an implementation plan for randomization hardening (value randomization + address-space coverage e.g. large malloc, offset randomization) that improves SDC detection coverage without breaking golden-value reproducibility.

## Next Step
User decision on the P1-P17 plan (approve / adjust priorities). After approval: rebase feat/sve-port-avx53 onto origin/main (d69ce8b2), then implement one patch unit at a time.

## Current Phase
Phase 5 (Delivery — presented 2026-09-20; baseline drift noted: tests/cpu/sve from PR #134-136 extends H9/H14 scope, ipsec datasize knob covers half of H6)

## Phases

### Phase 1: Test Audit (operand/address-space variation census)
- [x] Enumerate all test groups (301 files, ~308 test IDs across 30 dirs)
- [x] For each group: how are operands generated? (constant / fixed pattern / RNG per-thread / RNG per-run)
- [x] For each group: how is memory allocated? (static / stack / fixed malloc / sized malloc; single buffer vs multiple; offset randomization?)
- [x] Classify: which tests use random_input/randbits vs hardcoded constants
- [x] Check memory tests (memory/, cache/) for address-space coverage strategy
- [x] Document in findings.md (per-test table)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, 4 parallel audit agents)

### Phase 2: Framework capability survey
- [x] RNG facilities: random32/64/128, frandom*, memset_random, set_random_bits — per-thread streams, AES engine, -s reproducibility, fracture semantics
- [x] Memory allocation helpers: aligned_alloc_safe, ManagedCodeBuffer (RAII mmap), no THP helper needed (THP=always on host)
- [x] How golden-value comparison constrains randomization: all goldens runtime-computed (no source-hardcoded golden constants) → randomization fully compatible; golden must be same-run same-stream
- [x] Existing knobs: -O test.key=value + get_testspecific_knob_value_* (test_knobs.h); no generic --datasize
- [x] mmap/madvise/THP availability on the host: THP=always, ulimit unlimited, 52GB avail, kernel 6.6, device_info[].cache[] populated-but-unused, sysconf cache size broken (returns 0)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, framework survey agent + host probes)

### Phase 3: Gap analysis & hardening-point identification
- [x] Rank tests by (fixed operands, fixed addresses, small working set) — T0/T1/T2 classification in findings.md
- [x] For each hardening point: which randomization technique applies — H1..H15 table in findings.md
- [x] Identify tests where randomization breaks golden values: none (all goldens runtime-computed); constraint is only golden-recompute cost
- [x] Cross-reference 122-CPU SDC hunt mission context: clean-baseline gate + two-phase validation applies to all hardened/new tests
- **Status:** complete

### Phase 4: Plan formulation
- [x] Design common randomization helpers (if framework-level) vs per-test changes → decided: per-test changes using existing framework RNG + knobs; ONE new test (random_access_sweep); NO new framework surface
- [x] One-patch-per-unit decomposition matching CLAUDE.md patch discipline → P1..P17 units in final plan doc
- [x] Verification strategy per unit (build + run + regression + x86 non-regression + 122 two-phase for new tests)
- [x] Write final plan doc to docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-19-sdc-randomization-hardening.md
- **Status:** complete

### Phase 5: Delivery
- [ ] Present audit table + hardening points + plan to user
- [ ] Get approval / feedback
- **Status:** in_progress

## Decisions Made

# Task Plan: SDC Test Randomization Hardening (数值/地址空间变异加固)

## Goal
Audit all SDC detection tests for insufficient operand-value and address-space variation, identify hardening points, and produce an implementation plan for randomization hardening (value randomization + address-space coverage e.g. large malloc, offset randomization) that improves SDC detection coverage without breaking golden-value reproducibility.

## Next Step
User decision on the P1-P17 plan (approve / adjust priorities). After approval: rebase feat/sve-port-avx53 onto origin/main (d69ce8b2), then implement one patch unit at a time.

## Current Phase
Phase 5 (Delivery — presented 2026-09-20; baseline drift noted: tests/cpu/sve from PR #134-136 extends H9/H14 scope, ipsec datasize knob covers half of H6)

## Phases

### Phase 1: Test Audit (operand/address-space variation census)
- [x] Enumerate all test groups (301 files, ~308 test IDs across 30 dirs)
- [x] For each group: how are operands generated? (constant / fixed pattern / RNG per-thread / RNG per-run)
- [x] For each group: how is memory allocated? (static / stack / fixed malloc / sized malloc; single buffer vs multiple; offset randomization?)
- [x] Classify: which tests use random_input/randbits vs hardcoded constants
- [x] Check memory tests (memory/, cache/) for address-space coverage strategy
- [x] Document in findings.md (per-test table)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, 4 parallel audit agents)

### Phase 2: Framework capability survey
- [x] RNG facilities: random32/64/128, frandom*, memset_random, set_random_bits — per-thread streams, AES engine, -s reproducibility, fracture semantics
- [x] Memory allocation helpers: aligned_alloc_safe, ManagedCodeBuffer (RAII mmap), no THP helper needed (THP=always on host)
- [x] How golden-value comparison constrains randomization: all goldens runtime-computed (no source-hardcoded golden constants) → randomization fully compatible; golden must be same-run same-stream
- [x] Existing knobs: -O test.key=value + get_testspecific_knob_value_* (test_knobs.h); no generic --datasize
- [x] mmap/madvise/THP availability on the host: THP=always, ulimit unlimited, 52GB avail, kernel 6.6, device_info[].cache[] populated-but-unused, sysconf cache size broken (returns 0)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, framework survey agent + host probes)

28	**主体 = 狩猎 v3：2026-09-24 16:08:50 → 09-27 11:43:05 ALLDONE，连续 ~67.6h（67h34m）全核带载**（出处：`sdc_hunt_logs/2026-09-24-hunt-all128-122cap1450/STATUS.txt` 首末行）：
29	- 128 CPU 全核（cpu 0-127），**122 号核（= 旧122 = MPIDR 0x0900060200）全程在线并封顶 1.45 GHz**，封顶每项复检、丢失即中止；

34	- SVE 开发期（09-20~09-22）逐批两阶段验证为 60s 级短窗 × 数十批，无累计统计，不计入下述时长；

37	
38	## 二、哪些测试用例检出了 122 的 SDC
39	
40	**唯一检出：`movbe_dump_probe_c_sve`**（`tests/cpu/sve/core179/movbe_dump_probe_c_sve.cpp:135`；PROBE C——store-to-load forwarding 探针：svtbl [3,2,1,0] 字节交换 → svst1 直存堆 → svld1 立即重读同地址 → 第二次 svtbl 还原比对）。
41	
42	**检出事件（狩猎 v3 中，2026-09-26 21:39:06 起跑 → 22:19:06 窗口收割 rc=124）**，证据链（`movbe_dump_probe_c_sve.console` + coredump）：
43	- 框架自动重试 **3/3 全部失败，且三条记录全部仅 thread 122**（logical 122，package1/numa3/module36/**core292**，MPIDR 0x0900060200 与 STATUS 头部 journalctl 实证一致）；cpu-mask 128 位**仅 bit122 置位**，其余 127 线程全程干净；
44	- 三枚 SIGSEGV core 时间戳 **21:39:15 / 21:39:37 / 22:12:29**（PID 566021/566305/566623，同一二进制），到错间隔 9s → 22s → 32.9min；
45	- 数据错签名：index 10228（golden 0x8787532E → actual 0x5411F50C）、11604（0xD20EABE5 → 0x7BA2C0ED）两次位翻转 + index 12520（0x1D005B99 → 0x995B001D）**一次字节精确反转 = reload 拿回 store 前旧值 = store-to-load forwarding 失效**——正是 PROBE C 的设计目标；
46	- 同一事件还污染框架指针（故障指令 `ldrb w0,[x0,#9]` 读配置，x0 为未映射垃圾，三次 PC/FAR 相同）；种子 LCG:1883637953；
47	- **全程 122 封顶 1.45 GHz 生效中——降频不消除缺陷，只把到错间隔拉长**（对照：2.9 GHz 下 zstd19 秒级即崩）。
48	
49	代码同一性：该源文件最后一次提交为 09-21（7f8475d8），**检出后至今零改动**——后续所有复现尝试与检出时为同一份代码（复现用重建二进制 1023c841d414-dirty / f925888cae42-dirty，"-dirty" 来自其他文件改动）。
50	
51	对照组：同族 `movbe_sve`、`movbe_dump_sve`、probe_a/b/d/e/f/g1/g2/h/x/xn 共 12 个变体在 v3 及 09-29 家族顺序实验中**全部 pass**——probe_c 是唯一探测器。
52	
53	假阳性澄清（不属于"检出 122"）：`insert_extract_sve` 09-26 10:56:02–11:26:45 曾 FAIL（rc=139，sdc=1，summary.csv 实证），但命中 **CPU 7**（健康核满频区）而非 122；09-27 裁决为共享 `mem_buf` 128 线程竞态假阳性，**FAIL 撤销**，修复 commit 1023c841。**真 SDC 检出仅 122 一例。**
54	
55	## 三、检出之后又测了多长时间，没有复现 SDC
56	
57	**总跨度 2026-09-26 22:19 → 09-30 08:30（约 3.4 天），SDC 零复现。**分三类：
58	
59	**① 狩猎 v3 尾段：13.4h（09-26 22:19:06 → 09-27 11:43:05）**——probe_c 之后继续跑完剩余 **26 项** SVE 测试（probe_d/e/f/g1/g2/h/x/xn、mrn_* 系 6 个、neon_rot_2src、mite、partial_store_forwarding / agu_stress_2src / lsu_store_forward / l2c_cross_cache_line / mmu_split_tlb / ooo_dep_chain / arm64_sdc、gmp_bigadd / gmp_bignum / acl_gemm；STATUS.txt 逐项核实），全部 sdc=0。
60	
61	**② probe_c 本体定向复现 8 次合计 ~5.4h（322min），全部干净**：
62	
63	| 日期 | 运行 | 配置 | 结果 |
64	|---|---|---|---|
65	| 09-28 | 30min ×2 | 全核 0-127 | exit: pass ×2 |
66	| 09-28 | 2h | 全核 0-127 | exit: pass |
67	| 09-29 晨 | 原崩溃种子重放 30min | `-s LCG:1883637953`，全核 | exit: pass |
68	| 09-29 | 家族顺序实验中 probe_c 30min | 全核（movbe→dump→a→b→c 顺序） | exit: pass（5 项全 pass） |
69	| 09-29 晚 | 独跑 30min | **仅 122 单核** + 封顶 1.45GHz | rc=0，56 迭代全 pass，rng=AES |
70	| 09-29 晨 | matrix 组合 33.5min | 122 探针 + 127 核 stress-ng --matrix | **62/62 迭代 pass 后 122 挂死→2m21s 后内核 panic** |
71	| 09-30 晨 | vecfp 组合 18.5min | 122 探针 + 127 核 stress-ng --vecfp | **34/34 迭代 pass 后 122 挂死→2m08s 后内核 panic** |
72	
73	**③ 其他 SVE 测试**：09-28 ldr_at_top 对 2×30min、09-29 家族其余 4 项 4×30min，全部 pass。
74	
75	关键区分（诚实判读）：09-29/09-30 两次组合负载实验以**崩溃形态**终结——122 挂死（yaml 尾条目有 time-at-start 无 result）→ ~2 分钟后内核 panic（kdump 两枚 vmcore 940MB / 887MB，root-only 待归因）——**非 SDC 形态：全程零数据错，pass 计数干净**。两次组合（访存型 matrix、计算型 vecfp）与独跑 30min 干净的对照，指向"122 之外并发满载 + 122 探针"是硬崩溃的必要因子。
76	
77	未复现的判读：
78	- 符合 **SDC 偶然性原则**（概率事件，短窗采样不到）+ RNG 引擎每次运行随机选（random.cpp:603，跨运行 AES/LCG 差异正常）——原崩溃种子重放 30min 亦未复现，同种子 ≠ 同引擎路径；
79	- **未复现 ≠ 负载不能触发**；且组合负载下该核的失效形态已转移为硬崩溃（挂死→panic）。
80	
81	后续待办（均待裁决）：`movbe_slf_sweep_sve`（多宽度 SLF 变体）的 122 两阶段验证——应与 probe_c 同场同跑；两枚 vmcore 的 root 取证归因。

- **09-19~09-22 整周狩猎期间坏核被固件屏蔽 offline（127-CPU 启动）+ 编号漂移未察觉，全部负载实际落在健康核上**——该周数据点归属健康核对照基线（证明这些负载在好核上零误报）；
- **首次真正含坏核的 SVE 长测从 09-24 12:07 boot 起**（用户上线 122 + 封顶 1.45GHz）：09-24 冒烟 → 狩猎 v3（67.6h）→ 其后定向实验，至 09-30 08:30 数据截止点跨度约 5 天 20 小时（其间 09-29/09-30 两次组合负载实验触发整机 panic 并重启，见第三节）。

## 二、哪些测试用例检出了 122 的 SDC

**唯一检出：`movbe_dump_probe_c_sve`**（`tests/cpu/sve/core179/movbe_dump_probe_c_sve.cpp:135`；PROBE C——store-to-load forwarding 探针：svtbl [3,2,1,0] 字节交换 → svst1 直存堆 → svld1 立即重读同地址 → 第二次 svtbl 还原比对）。

**检出事件（狩猎 v3 中，2026-09-26 21:39:06 起跑 → 22:19:06 窗口收割 rc=124）**，证据链（`movbe_dump_probe_c_sve.console` + coredump）：
- 框架自动重试 **3/3 全部失败，且三条记录全部仅 thread 122**（logical 122，package1/numa3/module36/**core292**，MPIDR 0x0900060200 与 STATUS 头部 journalctl 实证一致）；cpu-mask 128 位**仅 bit122 置位**，其余 127 线程全程干净；
- 三枚 SIGSEGV core 时间戳 **21:39:15 / 21:39:37 / 22:12:29**（PID 566021/566305/566623，同一二进制），到错间隔 9s → 22s → 32.9min；
- 数据错签名：index 10228（golden 0x8787532E → actual 0x5411F50C）、11604（0xD20EABE5 → 0x7BA2C0ED）两次位翻转 + index 12520（0x1D005B99 → 0x995B001D）**一次字节精确反转 = reload 拿回 store 前旧值 = store-to-load forwarding 失效**——正是 PROBE C 的设计目标；
- 同一事件还污染框架指针（故障指令 `ldrb w0,[x0,#9]` 读配置，x0 为未映射垃圾，三次 PC/FAR 相同）；种子 LCG:1883637953；
- **全程 122 封顶 1.45 GHz 生效中——降频不消除缺陷，只把到错间隔拉长**（对照：2.9 GHz 下 zstd19 秒级即崩）。

代码同一性：该源文件最后一次提交为 09-21（7f8475d8），**检出后至今零改动**——后续所有复现尝试与检出时为同一份代码（复现用重建二进制 1023c841d414-dirty / f925888cae42-dirty，"-dirty" 来自其他文件改动）。

对照组：同族 `movbe_sve`、`movbe_dump_sve`、probe_a/b/d/e/f/g1/g2/h/x/xn 共 12 个变体在 v3 及 09-29 家族顺序实验中**全部 pass**——probe_c 是唯一探测器。

假阳性澄清（不属于"检出 122"）：`insert_extract_sve` 09-26 10:56:02–11:26:45 曾 FAIL（rc=139，sdc=1，summary.csv 实证），但命中 **CPU 7**（健康核满频区）而非 122；09-27 裁决为共享 `mem_buf` 128 线程竞态假阳性，**FAIL 撤销**，修复 commit 1023c841。**真 SDC 检出仅 122 一例。**

## 三、检出之后又测了多长时间，没有复现 SDC

**总跨度 2026-09-26 22:19 → 09-30 08:30（约 3.4 天），SDC 零复现。**分三类：

**① 狩猎 v3 尾段：13.4h（09-26 22:19:06 → 09-27 11:43:05）**——probe_c 之后继续跑完剩余 **26 项** SVE 测试（probe_d/e/f/g1/g2/h/x/xn、mrn_* 系 6 个、neon_rot_2src、mite、partial_store_forwarding / agu_stress_2src / lsu_store_forward / l2c_cross_cache_line / mmu_split_tlb / ooo_dep_chain / arm64_sdc、gmp_bigadd / gmp_bignum / acl_gemm；STATUS.txt 逐项核实），全部 sdc=0。

**② probe_c 本体定向复现 8 次合计 ~5.4h（322min），全部干净**：

| 日期 | 运行 | 配置 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 09-28 | 30min ×2 | 全核 0-127 | exit: pass ×2 |
| 09-28 | 2h | 全核 0-127 | exit: pass |
| 09-29 晨 | 原崩溃种子重放 30min | `-s LCG:1883637953`，全核 | exit: pass |
| 09-29 | 家族顺序实验中 probe_c 30min | 全核（movbe→dump→a→b→c 顺序） | exit: pass（5 项全 pass） |
| 09-29 晚 | 独跑 30min | **仅 122 单核** + 封顶 1.45GHz | rc=0，56 迭代全 pass，rng=AES |
| 09-29 晨 | matrix 组合 33.5min | 122 探针 + 127 核 stress-ng --matrix | **62/62 迭代 pass 后 122 挂死→2m21s 后内核 panic** |
| 09-30 晨 | vecfp 组合 18.5min | 122 探针 + 127 核 stress-ng --vecfp | **34/34 迭代 pass 后 122 挂死→2m08s 后内核 panic** |

**③ 其他 SVE 测试**：09-28 ldr_at_top 对 2×30min、09-29 家族其余 4 项 4×30min，全部 pass。

关键区分（诚实判读）：09-29/09-30 两次组合负载实验以**崩溃形态**终结——122 挂死（yaml 尾条目有 time-at-start 无 result）→ ~2 分钟后内核 panic（kdump 两枚 vmcore 940MB / 887MB，root-only 待归因）——**非 SDC 形态：全程零数据错，pass 计数干净**。两次组合（访存型 matrix、计算型 vecfp）与独跑 30min 干净的对照，指向"122 之外并发满载 + 122 探针"是硬崩溃的必要因子。

未复现的判读：
- 符合 **SDC 偶然性原则**（概率事件，短窗采样不到）+ RNG 引擎每次运行随机选（random.cpp:603，跨运行 AES/LCG 差异正常）——原崩溃种子重放 30min 亦未复现，同种子 ≠ 同引擎路径；
- **未复现 ≠ 负载不能触发**；且组合负载下该核的失效形态已转移为硬崩溃（挂死→panic）。

后续待办（均待裁决）：`movbe_slf_sweep_sve`（多宽度 SLF 变体）的 122 两阶段验证——应与 probe_c 同场同跑；两枚 vmcore 的 root 取证归因。

已经把过程完整还原了。以下是 SVE 类测试用例扩展的全程回顾（依据 git log、`docs/docs_xu/` 系列文档与狩猎日志逐项核实）：

## 一、起点：能力研究与可转性分析（09-18 ~ 09-20）

- `2026-09-18-sve-capability-research.md` — 先摸清 SVE 硬件能力边界；
- `2026-09-20-95tests-sve-improvability-analysis.md`（v1+v2）— 对全仓库测试做“能转未转”普查，得出 **64 个可转换清单**，成为后续批次的依据。工作分支就是现在的 `feat/sve-port-avx53`。

## 二、第一波：avx53 移植（09-20，53 个）

把 53 个 avx 命名的 NEON 测试做 SVE 版（PR #134–137/#140/#141，`47a7b344` 建目录骨架）：FMA 10、Mesh 18、eigen 1、IPSec 24。支撑资产 `sve_sha_kernels.h` / `sve_hmac.h`（多流 SVE SHA/HMAC 内核，OpenSSL 比对 5200/5200、1360/1360）也在这一波落地。

## 三、第二波：64 转换计划分 7 批（09-21，一个周末完成）

| 批次 | 主题 | 数量 |
|---|---|---|
| 批1 | kreg 软件仿真 → 真 SVE 谓词指令 | 7 |
| 批2 | NEON intrinsic 直换 | 13 |
| 批3+4 | 换算类 + 进位链/大数 | 12 |
| 批5 | core-179 数据流族（movbe/probe ×11/mrn ×6…） | 21 |
| 批6 | 谓词部分写 + AGU/LSU/L2C/MMU/OOO 访存压测 | 7 |
| 批7 | 库负载 SVE 自实现（gmp/acl） | 3+1 gated |

批5 还带一次**保真修复**（`7f8475d8`）：movbe 族的 store/reload 改为直落堆内存。当日完成**四标准审计**（随机性/SIMD/浮点范围/日志），锁定清单 **117 源文件 / 116 注册**（`crt_builtins_sve` 因本机无 libclang_rt 与原版同 gate 未构建）。

## 四、质量纪律：每批两阶段验证

每批都走 122 核流程：阶段1 `--cpuset='!122'` 零 fail 证明逻辑正确 → 阶段2 全核含 122 观察触发，累计数据点 #1–#11。
**事后诚实修正**（9-30 总结文档）：09-19~09-22 那周坏核实际被固件 offline（127-CPU 启动）+ 编号漂移未察觉，两阶段验证的负载其实全落在健康核上——该周数据点的真实价值是“这些负载在好核上零误报”；首次真正含坏核的 SVE 长测从 09-24 12:07 boot 起。

## 五、长测验证：狩猎 v3（09-24 16:08 → 09-27 11:43，~67.6h）

128 核全核、122 封顶 1.45 GHz、116 项 × 30min。结果：**`movbe_dump_probe_c_sve` 唯一真检出**——3/3 重试全失败且全部仅 thread 122，签名正是其设计目标（store-to-load forwarding 失效：index 12520 字节精确反转 = reload 拿回 store 前旧值），同场还污染框架指针 SIGSEGV。另一 FAIL `insert_extract_sve`（命中 CPU 7）后裁决为共享 `mem_buf` 128 线程竞态**假阳性**，修复 `1023c841`。

## 六、检出后的定向扩展（09-28 → 120 个）

基于 probe_c 的发现追加：`movbe_slf_sweep_sve`（d90777cf，多宽度 16/32/64-bit SLF 往返探针）+ `neon_rot_ldr_at_top` 对移植 SVE（14a82a92）→ **tests/cpu/sve/ 最终 120 个**（全仓库 SVE 测试名合计 131 = 120 + 既有 11 个）。检出后 ~3.4 天定向复现（8 次 probe_c 共 ~5.4h + 家族对照）零复现，但 09-29/09-30 两次组合负载实验以硬崩溃形态（122 挂死→panic）终结。

## 七、过程踩的坑（都已修复入档）

- gcc-10 三个 ICE：svst1 地址含 `&` 常数（`0d9c04aa`）、probe f/g1/g2 RTL expand（`67007a45`，函数级 O1 绕过）、gcc-16.2 mesh_upi_sve_asymm_int（`14e85c80`，函数级 O0）；
- sanitizer 豁免（`45478943`）、sve512 族 VL/预算 gate（`ce9b5fc4`，issue #182）。

## 八、后续延伸（09-30 之后，同一思路的延续）

ctx 系列上下文仿真压测（`libomp_ctx_arm`、`sve512_xlswave_ctx_arm`、`sme_za_tileview_arm`）；10-09 全核心 @2.0GHz 频率批中 **`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_sve` 成为第二个锁定 122 的测试**（全核心方法论首验）、`movbe_dump_probe_x` 第三个（首个非 SVE 锁定测试）。

一句话总结：**研究普查 → avx53 移植 53 + 分 7 批转换 64 → 四标准审计 + 两阶段验证 → 67.6h 全核狩猎检出去 122 → 按检出签名定向扩展至 120**，全程一波三折但每一步都有日志和 commit 佐证。

# Task Plan: SDC Test Randomization Hardening (数值/地址空间变异加固)

## Goal
Audit all SDC detection tests for insufficient operand-value and address-space variation, identify hardening points, and produce an implementation plan for randomization hardening (value randomization + address-space coverage e.g. large malloc, offset randomization) that improves SDC detection coverage without breaking golden-value reproducibility.

## Next Step
User decision on the P1-P17 plan (approve / adjust priorities). After approval: rebase feat/sve-port-avx53 onto origin/main (d69ce8b2), then implement one patch unit at a time.

## Current Phase
Phase 5 (Delivery — presented 2026-09-20; baseline drift noted: tests/cpu/sve from PR #134-136 extends H9/H14 scope, ipsec datasize knob covers half of H6)

## Phases

### Phase 1: Test Audit (operand/address-space variation census)
- [x] Enumerate all test groups (301 files, ~308 test IDs across 30 dirs)
- [x] For each group: how are operands generated? (constant / fixed pattern / RNG per-thread / RNG per-run)
- [x] For each group: how is memory allocated? (static / stack / fixed malloc / sized malloc; single buffer vs multiple; offset randomization?)
- [x] Classify: which tests use random_input/randbits vs hardcoded constants
- [x] Check memory tests (memory/, cache/) for address-space coverage strategy
- [x] Document in findings.md (per-test table)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, 4 parallel audit agents)

### Phase 2: Framework capability survey
- [x] RNG facilities: random32/64/128, frandom*, memset_random, set_random_bits — per-thread streams, AES engine, -s reproducibility, fracture semantics
- [x] Memory allocation helpers: aligned_alloc_safe, ManagedCodeBuffer (RAII mmap), no THP helper needed (THP=always on host)
- [x] How golden-value comparison constrains randomization: all goldens runtime-computed (no source-hardcoded golden constants) → randomization fully compatible; golden must be same-run same-stream
- [x] Existing knobs: -O test.key=value + get_testspecific_knob_value_* (test_knobs.h); no generic --datasize
- [x] mmap/madvise/THP availability on the host: THP=always, ulimit unlimited, 52GB avail, kernel 6.6, device_info[].cache[] populated-but-unused, sysconf cache size broken (returns 0)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, framework survey agent + host probes)


===END-PWF-DATA kind=plan nonce=9d034067a2c41ecc834063b4==="}}

## Goal
Audit all SDC detection tests for insufficient operand-value and address-space variation, identify hardening points, and produce an implementation plan for randomization hardening (value randomization + address-space coverage e.g. large malloc, offset randomization) that improves SDC detection coverage without breaking golden-value reproducibility.

## Next Step
User decision on the P1-P17 plan (approve / adjust priorities). After approval: rebase feat/sve-port-avx53 onto origin/main (d69ce8b2), then implement one patch unit at a time.

Phase 5 (Delivery — presented 2026-09-20; baseline drift noted: tests/cpu/sve from PR #134-136 extends H9/H14 scope, ipsec datasize knob covers half of H6)

## Phases

### Phase 1: Test Audit (operand/address-space variation census)
- [x] Enumerate all test groups (301 files, ~308 test IDs across 30 dirs)
- [x] For each group: how are operands generated? (constant / fixed pattern / RNG per-thread / RNG per-run)
- [x] For each group: how is memory allocated? (static / stack / fixed malloc / sized malloc; single buffer vs multiple; offset randomization?)
- [x] Classify: which tests use random_input/randbits vs hardcoded constants
- [x] Check memory tests (memory/, cache/) for address-space coverage strategy
- [x] Document in findings.md (per-test table)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, 4 parallel audit agents)

### Phase 2: Framework capability survey
- [x] RNG facilities: random32/64/128, frandom*, memset_random, set_random_bits — per-thread streams, AES engine, -s reproducibility, fracture semantics
- [x] Memory allocation helpers: aligned_alloc_safe, ManagedCodeBuffer (RAII mmap), no THP helper needed (THP=always on host)
- [x] How golden-value comparison constrains randomization: all goldens runtime-computed (no source-hardcoded golden constants) → randomization fully compatible; golden must be same-run same-stream

- [x] mmap/madvise/THP availability on the host: THP=always, ulimit unlimited, 52GB avail, kernel 6.6, device_info[].cache[] populated-but-unused, sysconf cache size broken (returns 0)
- **Status:** complete (2026-09-19, framework survey agent + host probes)

All 4 files read completely. Summary below. One upfront correction to the premise: **these tests contain no NEON intrinsics and no SIMD at all** — every memory op is scalar 64-bit `str`/`ldr` inline asm on ARM64. Also, the actual total is **11 tests, not 12** (your list of 11 names matches exactly what exists; a 12th test `mrn_rmw_diff_nop64` is *referenced* in comments in file 4 but is not defined in any of these files).

All tests are one family: probes for a load-pathway SDC on "core-179" of the sister machine, built around the same skeleton (ALU op on random srcA/srcB → `str` to temp → `ldr` reload → compare vs runtime-computed golden). The design comments repeatedly stress that *any* perturbation of the hot loop (even cold branches) can silence the timing-sensitive defect, so SVE ports should preserve instruction sequence/count exactly.

---

## File 1: `mrn_rmw_fwd_vs_l1d.cpp` (2 tests)

**Shared code (file-level):**
- `struct MrnRmwData { uint64_t *srcA, *srcB, *expected; }`
- Helpers (all inside `#if defined(__aarch64__)`, **no non-aarch64 fallback**):
```c
static inline void store_qword(void *addr, uint64_t val) {
    __asm__ volatile ("str %1, [%0]" : : "r"(addr), "r"(val) : "memory"); }
static inline uint64_t load_qword(const void *addr) {
    uint64_t res; __asm__ volatile ("ldr %0, [%1]" : "=r"(res) : "r"(addr) : "memory"); return res; }
static inline void evict_l1d_line(const void *addr) {
    __asm__ volatile("dc civac, %0\n\tdsb sy\n\t" :: "r"(addr) : "memory"); }
```
- `mrn_rmw_probe_init` / `mrn_rmw_probe_cleanup` — shared by both tests.
- `log_miscompare(tag, i, op, inputA, inputB, golden, actual)` — shared cold-path logger: `log_error` with golden/actual/xor in hex + byte-by-byte b7..b0, then `report_fail_msg(...)` (noreturn → only first mismatch per thread ever logs).
- `#define MRN_RMW_COUNT 1024` (8 KB per buffer).

**Shared init (`mrn_rmw_probe_init`):** `malloc` the struct; 3× `aligned_alloc(64, 8192)` for srcA/srcB/expected; `memset_random` on srcA and srcB; golden loop: `switch (i % 4)` → `expected[i] = srcA[i] + - ^ & srcB[i]` (case 0=add, 1=sub, 2=xor, 3=and); `test->data = data`.

**Shared cleanup:** frees the 3 buffers + struct.

### Test 1: `mrn_rmw_fwd`
- **description:** `"mrn_rmw load-path probe (store-buffer FORWARDING): str then ldr same addr — core-179 SDC expected"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups:** not set (default); **flags:** not set.
- **preinit/init/run/cleanup:** preinit NULL; init = shared `mrn_rmw_probe_init`; run = `mrn_rmw_fwd_run`; cleanup = shared `mrn_rmw_probe_cleanup`.
- **memory:** srcA/srcB/expected in `test->data` — **shared across all per-CPU threads, but read-only after init** (written only in init before workers spawn) → no race. `temp` and `dst` are `aligned_alloc(64, 8192)` **inside run → per-thread, private**, freed at end of run. No race risk (this is the safe pattern, unlike the insert_extract_sve shared-buffer bug).
- **core loop:** `TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13)` (max 8192 time-bounded passes) over 1024 elements:
```c
uint64_t a = data->srcA[i];  uint64_t b = data->srcB[i];
switch (i % 4) { case 0: res = a + b; case 1: res = a - b; case 2: res = a ^ b; default: res = a & b; }
store_qword(&temp[i], res);
store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword(&temp[i]));   // str temp[i] -> ldr SAME addr -> str dst[i]
```
Probes **store-buffer store-to-load forwarding** (load of just-stored same address served from store buffer, bypassing the L1D read array). Byte-identical to the original `mrn_rmw.cpp` hot loop; expected to trigger the SDC (historically ~15 fails/10min per file-2 header).
- **verification:** once per full pass (after the 1024-element inner loop, inside TEST_LOOP): `memcmp(dst, data->expected, 8192)`; on mismatch, scan all i and call `log_miscompare("mrn_rmw_fwd", ...)` (noreturn inside).
- **RNG:** `memset_random` on srcA/srcB in init only (framework per-run engine/seed, drawn once on the child main thread); no `random_input`/`randbits`, no explicit seeds, no RNG in run.
- **special:** no knobs, no sleeps, no fprintf. Timing-sensitive by design (str→ldr back-to-back, volatile asm + "memory" clobber prevent reordering).

### Test 2: `mrn_rmw_l1d`
- **description:** `"mrn_rmw load-path probe (L1D-array read): evict between str and ldr — distinguishes forwarding vs L1D array"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups/flags:** not set.
- **preinit/init/run/cleanup:** init/cleanup shared as above; run = `mrn_rmw_l1d_run`.
- **memory:** identical to `mrn_rmw_fwd` (shared read-only inputs; per-thread temp/dst in run).
- **core loop:** identical to `mrn_rmw_fwd` **except** one inserted line between the two stores:
```c
store_qword(&temp[i], res);
evict_l1d_line(&temp[i]);                     // dc civac + dsb sy, per element
store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword(&temp[i]));
```
Forces the reload to be served from the L1D array / further (store flushed) instead of forwarding. `dc civac; dsb sy` runs **per element** (1024× per pass — very slow per pass). Note: `civac` clean+invalidate to PoC means the reload likely actually misses L1D and comes from L2 — the code comment says "L1D array (or further)".
- **verification:** same batched memcmp + `log_miscompare("mrn_rmw_l1d", ...)` per pass.
- **RNG:** same as fwd.
- **special:** `dc civac`/`dsb sy` are aarch64 system instructions — nothing SVE-specific, but non-portable off ARM64.

---

## File 2: `mrn_rmw_fwd_vs_diff.cpp` (1 test)

**Shared code:** `struct MrnRmwDiffData { uint64_t *srcA, *srcB, *expected, *tempA, *tempB; }`; `store_qword`/`load_qword` helpers (same inline asm as file 1, no `evict_l1d_line`). Single test — no sharing across tests. `MRN_RMW_COUNT 1024`.

### Test 3: `mrn_rmw_diff`
- **description:** `"mrn_rmw forward-isolation probe: str to tempA then ldr from DIFFERENT addr tempB (L1D-array, not forwarding) — isolates forwarding path"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups/flags:** not set.
- **preinit:** NULL; **init:** `mrn_rmw_diff_init`; **run:** `mrn_rmw_diff_run`; **cleanup:** `mrn_rmw_diff_cleanup`.
- **memory:** init mallocs struct + 5× `aligned_alloc(64, 8192)`: srcA, srcB, expected, **tempA, tempB — all in `test->data`, shared across threads**. tempB pre-filled with `expected[i]`, tempA zeroed. **Race assessment:** tempA is *written* by every worker thread every pass — but every thread writes the identical value (deterministic function of read-only srcA/srcB) to the same aligned 64-bit address, and **no thread ever reads tempA**; verification reads only tempB/expected (read-only after init). Benign same-value race in practice (aligned 64-bit stores are single-copy atomic on ARMv8); no false-positive mechanism. Still worth documenting in a port — but note the header's warning that changing the hot loop can silence the defect.
- **core loop:** `TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13)`, per element: same ALU switch, then
```c
store_qword(&data->tempA[i], res);
uint64_t got = load_qword(&data->tempB[i]);   // DIFFERENT address — L1D-array read, not forwarding
```
Keeps the tight str→ldr pair (same instruction count/time gap as fwd) but changes only the **load address**, so forwarding is impossible (store wrote tempA, not tempB) — isolates "forwarding path" vs "str→ldr proximity/timing". No dst buffer, no allocation in run.
- **verification:** **per-element, immediately inside the hot loop** (unlike files 1/4): `if (got != data->expected[i])` → inline `log_error` (golden/actual/xor hex + bytes b7..b0) + `report_fail_msg` (noreturn). Cold branch only.
- **RNG:** `memset_random` on srcA/srcB in init; expected/tempB derived. Nothing in run.
- **special:** no knobs/sleeps/fprintf. The op-name string for logs is computed via nested ternary on `i % 4`.

---

## File 3: `mrn_rmw_diff_footprint.cpp` (2 tests)

**Shared code (file-level):**
- `#define MRN_RMW_DIFF_64K_COUNT 8192` (64 KB == L1D, thrash edge) / `#define MRN_RMW_DIFF_1M_COUNT 131072` (1 MB = 16× L1D).
- `struct MrnRmwDiffFpData` = MrnRmwDiffData **plus `int count`**.
- `store_qword`/`load_qword` (same as before).
- `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_init_common(struct test *test, int count)` — parameterized init (identical body to file 2's init but count-sized, including tempB pre-fill with golden and tempA zeroing); thin wrappers `mrn_rmw_diff_64k_init` / `mrn_rmw_diff_1m_init` pass the two constants.
- `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_cleanup` — shared by both.
- **`mrn_rmw_diff_fp_run` — ONE shared run function for BOTH tests**; distinguishes itself via `const char *tag = test->id;` and `int count = data->count;`. Body byte-identical to file 2's run (str tempA → ldr tempB → per-element verify) with tag/count substituted.

### Test 4: `mrn_rmw_diff_64k`
- **description:** `"mrn_rmw footprint probe (L1D thrash edge): diff-addr str->ldr, tempB=64KB==L1D — does L1D-array read trigger at thrash edge?"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups/flags:** not set.
- **preinit:** NULL; **init:** `mrn_rmw_diff_64k_init` → common(8192); **run:** shared `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_run`; **cleanup:** shared.
- **memory:** 5 buffers × 64 KB (320 KB total) in `test->data`, shared; same benign same-value tempA race as file 2. No per-thread allocation in run.
- **core loop:** identical to `mrn_rmw_diff` but 8192 elements/pass. Probes whether the L1D-array-read trigger rate changes when the tempB stream exactly fills L1D (1024 lines → 256 sets × 4 ways, capacity/thrash edge).
- **verification:** per-element `got != expected[i]` inside the loop, `log_error` with `tag` + `report_fail_msg` (noreturn). Cold branch.
- **RNG:** `memset_random` on count-sized srcA/srcB in init.
- **special:** none beyond the shared design.

### Test 5: `mrn_rmw_diff_1m`
- Same as `_64k` except: **init** = `mrn_rmw_diff_1m_init` → common(131072); **description:** `"mrn_rmw footprint probe (L2-reload): diff-addr str->ldr, tempB=1MB=16xL1D — every reload misses L1D (served from L2). If SDC needs L1D hit, should vanish."`; **run/cleanup shared with _64k**.
- **memory:** 5 buffers × 1 MB (5 MB total) shared. Every tempB reload misses L1D → L2/L3 refill path; only variable vs `_64k` is buffer size.

---

## File 4: `mrn_rmw_timing_probe.cpp` (6 tests)

**Shared code (file-level):**
- `#define MRN_RMW_COUNT 1024`; `struct MrnRmwData` (same 3-field shape as file 1); `store_qword`/`load_qword` (same asm).
- **Six delayed-load helpers**, each = N data-independent ALU no-ops (`mov x9, x9`) before the `ldr`, emitted via `.rept N ... .endr`:
```c
static inline uint64_t load_qword_delayed(const void *addr) {   // N=2 (used by mrn_rmw_nop)
    uint64_t res;
    __asm__ volatile(".rept 2\n\tmov x9, x9\n\t.endr\n\tldr %0, [%1]"
                     : "=r"(res) : "r"(addr) : "memory");
    return res; }
```
Variants: `load_qword_delayed` (2), `..._delayed1` (1), `..._delayed4` (4), `..._delayed8` (8), `..._delayed16` (16), `..._delayed64` (64). All keep the **same-address forwarding path** (nothing evicts the store; only the str→ldr time gap widens). Note: `mov x9, x9` uses hard register x9 without declaring it in the clobber list — semantically a value-preserving no-op so harmless, but a port caution.
- `mrn_rmw_nop_init` / `mrn_rmw_nop_cleanup` — **shared by all 6 tests**; body identical to file 1's `mrn_rmw_probe_init`/`cleanup` (3× 8 KB buffers, memset_random, i%4 golden).
- **Six DISTINCT run functions** (`mrn_rmw_nop_run`, `nop1_run`, `nop4_run`, `nop8_run`, `nop16_run`, `nop64_run`) — copy-paste clones differing in exactly two things: which `load_qword_delayedN` is called, and the hardcoded tag string in the log messages. No shared/tag-driven runner (unlike file 3).

### Test 6: `mrn_rmw_nop` (the 2-no-op point)
- **description:** `"mrn_rmw timing-only probe: 2 ALU no-ops between str and ldr (forwarding path kept, store buffer undrained) - bisects the 1..64 cycle race window (nop1=1fail, nop64=0fail)"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups/flags:** not set.
- **preinit:** NULL; **init:** shared `mrn_rmw_nop_init`; **run:** `mrn_rmw_nop_run`; **cleanup:** shared `mrn_rmw_nop_cleanup`.
- **memory:** identical to `mrn_rmw_fwd`: srcA/srcB/expected shared read-only; `temp`/`dst` `aligned_alloc(64, 8192)` per-thread in run, freed at end. No race.
- **core loop:** `TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13)`; per element: same ALU switch, then
```c
store_qword(&temp[i], res);
store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword_delayed(&temp[i]));   // 2 no-ops between str and ldr
```
Probes the **width of the str→ldr race window** on the forwarding path (~2-cycle gap; historically nop2 = 6 fails).
- **verification:** batched per pass: `memcmp(dst, expected, 8192)` then per-mismatch scan with inline `log_error` (inputA/inputB/golden/actual/xor + bytes) and `report_fail_msg("mrn_rmw_nop: ...")` (noreturn).
- **RNG:** `memset_random` on srcA/srcB in init only.
- **special:** `.rept`/`.endr` GNU-as directives (fine under GCC/Clang aarch64); gap series is cycle-calibrated to the original core — the most timing-sensitive file.

### Tests 7–11: `mrn_rmw_nop1`, `nop4`, `nop8`, `nop16`, `nop64`
Each is **structurally identical to `mrn_rmw_nop`** (same shared init/cleanup, same memory layout, same batched memcmp verification, same RNG usage, same no-knobs/no-sleep profile). Deltas only:

| test | run fn | helper (gap) | description (key part) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mrn_rmw_nop1` | `mrn_rmw_nop1_run` | `load_qword_delayed1` (1 no-op, ~1 cycle) | re-creates the missing ~1-cycle point of the fwd(0)/nop1(1)/nop(2) gap series; historically 1 fail/10min |
| `mrn_rmw_nop4` | `mrn_rmw_nop4_run` | `load_qword_delayed4` (4) | extends series past the non-monotonic 1→2 rise (nop1=0, nop2=6) |
| `mrn_rmw_nop8` | `mrn_rmw_nop8_run` | `load_qword_delayed8` (8) | traces descent from ~2-cycle peak toward nop64=0 plateau; nop8 30min = 0 fail |
| `mrn_rmw_nop16` | `mrn_rmw_nop16_run` | `load_qword_delayed16` (16) | between 4-cycle residual (~1) and 64-cycle 0-plateau; designed for long (1 h) runs |
| `mrn_rmw_nop64` | `mrn_rmw_nop64_run` | `load_qword_delayed64` (64) | same-address cell of a 2×2 timing matrix; historically 0 fail/364 iters; pairs with (absent) `mrn_rmw_diff_nop64` to decide path-switch vs timing-window |

All `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`, groups/flags/preinit not set. Log tag strings are hardcoded per test (e.g. `"mrn_rmw_nop4: miscompare at index %u ..."`).

---

## Complete test list (11, not 12)

1. `mrn_rmw_fwd` — file 1
2. `mrn_rmw_l1d` — file 1
3. `mrn_rmw_diff` — file 2
4. `mrn_rmw_diff_64k` — file 3
5. `mrn_rmw_diff_1m` — file 3
6. `mrn_rmw_nop` — file 4
7. `mrn_rmw_nop1` — file 4
8. `mrn_rmw_nop4` — file 4
9. `mrn_rmw_nop8` — file 4
10. `mrn_rmw_nop16` — file 4
11. `mrn_rmw_nop64` — file 4

`mrn_rmw_diff_nop64` (different-address + 64-no-op cell of the 2×2 matrix) is referenced in the `mrn_rmw_nop64` description/comments but **does not exist in these 4 files** — if it exists at all, it is elsewhere; it is the natural "missing 12th" test.

## Shared vs distinct test_run

- **Shared run function:** `mrn_rmw_diff_64k` and `mrn_rmw_diff_1m` both use `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_run` (parameterized by `test->id` tag + `data->count`).
- **Distinct run functions:** everything else. `mrn_rmw_fwd_run` vs `mrn_rmw_l1d_run` differ by one `evict_l1d_line` call. File 4's six run functions are textual clones differing only in the `load_qword_delayedN` call and hardcoded log tag — a port could consolidate them file-3-style (tag via `test->id`, gap via a parameter), at the cost of no longer being byte-identical to the originals.
- **Shared init/cleanup:** file 1 both tests (`mrn_rmw_probe_init`/`cleanup`); file 3 both tests (`mrn_rmw_diff_fp_init_common` via wrappers + `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_cleanup`); file 4 all six tests (`mrn_rmw_nop_init`/`cleanup`); file 2 standalone.

## Key port notes for SVE versions

- No SIMD anywhere today: scalar `str`/`ldr` qword inline asm + scalar ALU. An "SVE port" is either (a) re-homing these as-is, or (b) new `st1d`/`ld1d`-based variants of the same forwarding/timing/footprint design (vector store→same-address vector load exercises the same store-buffer forwarding with different uop shapes).
- The invariant that matters: **str→ldr address relationship, instruction count between them, and the i%4 ALU-op mix** (init and run must stay in sync). Header comments warn even cold-branch changes silenced the defect.
- Non-portable/off-ARM pieces: `dc civac`, `dsb sy`, `.rept/.endr`, `mov x9,x9` (x9 not in clobber list — benign but note it). Helpers are inside `#if defined(__aarch64__)` with **no fallback**, so the files only compile on aarch64.
- Race safety: files 1/4 are clean (per-thread temp/dst in run). Files 2/3 share writable tempA across threads, but all threads store identical values and never read it back — benign in practice, but a port should either document this or (carefully) keep it for hot-loop fidelity.
- All verification goldens are runtime-computed (no hardcoded constants) → fully compatible with the framework's per-run random engine/seed; `memset_random` is called once per test in init (child main thread), so all threads see identical inputs.

```c
static inline void store_qword(void *addr, uint64_t val) {
    __asm__ volatile ("str %1, [%0]" : : "r"(addr), "r"(val) : "memory"); }
static inline uint64_t load_qword(const void *addr) {
    uint64_t res; __asm__ volatile ("ldr %0, [%1]" : "=r"(res) : "r"(addr) : "memory"); return res; }
static inline void evict_l1d_line(const void *addr) {
```

- **description:** `"mrn_rmw load-path probe (store-buffer FORWARDING): str then ldr same addr — core-179 SDC expected"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups:** not set (default); **flags:** not set.

No race risk (this is the safe pattern, unlike the insert_extract_sve shared-buffer bug).
- **core loop:** `TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13)` (max 8192 time-bounded passes) over 1024 elements:
```c
uint64_t a = data->srcA[i];  uint64_t b = data->srcB[i];
switch (i % 4) { case 0: res = a + b; case 1: res = a - b; case 2: res = a ^ b; default: res = a & b; }
store_qword(&temp[i], res);
store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword(&temp[i]));   // str temp[i] -> ldr SAME addr -> str dst[i]
```

```c

evict_l1d_line(&temp[i]);                     // dc civac + dsb sy, per element
store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword(&temp[i]));
```
Forces the reload to be served from the L1D array / further (store flushed) instead of forwarding. `dc civac; dsb sy` runs **per element** (1024× per pass — very slow per pass). Note: `civac` clean+invalidate to PoC means the reload likely actually misses L1D and comes from L2 — the code comment says "L1D array (or further)".

- **description:** `"mrn_rmw forward-isolation probe: str to tempA then ldr from DIFFERENT addr tempB (L1D-array, not forwarding) — isolates forwarding path"`; **quality_level:** `TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **groups/flags:** not set.

Still worth documenting in a port — but note the header's warning that changing the hot loop can silence the defect.

```c
store_qword(&data->tempA[i], res);
uint64_t got = load_qword(&data->tempB[i]);   // DIFFERENT address — L1D-array read, not forwarding
```
Keeps the tight str→ldr pair (same instruction count/time gap as fwd) but changes only the **load address**, so forwarding is impossible (store wrote tempA, not tempB) — isolates "forwarding path" vs "str→ldr proximity/timing". No dst buffer, no allocation in run.


```c
store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword_delayed(&temp[i]));   // 2 no-ops between str and ldr
```

1. `mrn_rmw_fwd` — file 1
2. `mrn_rmw_l1d` — file 1
3. `mrn_rmw_diff` — file 2
4. `mrn_rmw_diff_64k` — file 3
5. `mrn_rmw_diff_1m` — file 3

8. `mrn_rmw_nop4` — file 4

## Shared vs distinct test_run

- **Shared run function:** `mrn_rmw_diff_64k` and `mrn_rmw_diff_1m` both use `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_run` (parameterized by `test->id` tag + `data->count`).
- **Distinct run functions:** everything else. `mrn_rmw_fwd_run` vs `mrn_rmw_l1d_run` differ by one `evict_l1d_line` call. File 4's six run functions are textual clones differing only in the `load_qword_delayedN` call and hardcoded log tag — a port could consolidate them file-3-style (tag via `test->id`, gap via a parameter), at the cost of no longer being byte-identical to the originals.
- **Shared init/cleanup:** file 1 both tests (`mrn_rmw_probe_init`/`cleanup`); file 3 both tests (`mrn_rmw_diff_fp_init_common` via wrappers + `mrn_rmw_diff_fp_cleanup`); file 4 all six tests (`mrn_rmw_nop_init`/`cleanup`); file 2 standalone.

## Key port notes for SVE versions

- No SIMD anywhere today: scalar `str`/`ldr` qword inline asm + scalar ALU. An "SVE port" is either (a) re-homing these as-is, or (b) new `st1d`/`ld1d`-based variants of the same forwarding/timing/footprint design (vector store→same-address vector load exercises the same store-buffer forwarding with different uop shapes).
- The invariant that matters: **str→ldr address relationship, instruction count between them, and the i%4 ALU-op mix** (init and run must stay in sync). Header comments warn even cold-branch changes silenced the defect.
- Non-portable/off-ARM pieces: `dc civac`, `dsb sy`, `.rept/.endr`, `mov x9,x9` (x9 not in clobber list — benign but note it). Helpers are inside `#if defined(__aarch64__)` with **no fallback**, so the files only compile on aarch64.
- Race safety: files 1/4 are clean (per-thread temp/dst in run). Files 2/3 share writable tempA across threads, but all threads store identical values and never read it back — benign in practice, but a port should either document this or (carefully) keep it for hot-loop fidelity.
- All verification goldens are runtime-computed (no hardcoded constants) → fully compatible with the framework's per-run random engine/seed; `memset_random` is called once per test in init (child main thread), so all threads see identical inputs.

  ```c
  val = __builtin_bswap32(val);           // reverse back
  ```

# How similar are mrn_nuke_2src/3src/4src?

**They are three instantiations of a single template — yes, systematic variations of one file.** Everything is byte-identical modulo renaming: the `store_qword`/`load_qword` asm helpers, the `init` flow (malloc struct → `aligned_alloc(64, COUNT*8)` sources → `memset_random` → precompute `expected[]`), the `run` flow (per-thread `temp`+`dst` alloc → `TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13)` → inner 1024-element loop with `i % 4` switch → skeleton `store_qword(&temp[i], res); store_qword(&dst[i], load_qword(&temp[i]));` → bulk `memcmp` → `report_fail_msg` → free), and `cleanup`. The ONLY differences:

1. **Source count / struct fields**: 2 (`srcA,srcB`) / 3 (`+srcC`) / 4 (`+srcD`) — dependency-chain depth 1 / 2 / 3.
2. **The ALU rotation expressions** (the actual experimental variable):
   - 2src: `a+b, a-b, a^b, a&b`
   - 3src: `a^b^c, (a+b)^c, a^(b+c), (a^b)+c`
   - 4src: `a^b^c^d, ((a+b)^c)+d, (a^b)+(c^d), a^(b+c)^d`
3. Identifiers, fail-message strings, test name/description.

Notably, **`mrn_pairs_2src_alu` is also code-identical to `mrn_nuke_2src_alu`** (same struct shape, same `{+,-,^,&}` rotation, same skeleton, same TEST_LOOP count) — its distinct identity is purely lineage (variant of `mrn_pairs`, collapsed 8+8 unroll) and naming. `mrn_reloaded_2src_alu` shares the init/ALU half but diverges in run (no `dst`, `TEST_LOOP 1<<8`, immediate per-element compare). `mrn_nuke_dense` shares the skeleton but drops ALU/sources and scales COUNT 1024→16384. So a port of this family can be built from one parameterized template with per-variant: source count, ALU rotation table, element count, verification mode (bulk memcmp vs immediate), and reload presence (store→load→store vs store-only). The porting-relevant axes across the whole family are: reload present (mrn_nuke 2/3/4src, pairs, reloaded) vs absent (agu, neon_rot), ALU before store (all except dense/movbe), fixed stride (all except mem_disambig_alu) vs random address, bulk vs immediate verification, and scalar u64 vs NEON u64x2 datapath.

All 13 files read in full. Below is the structured summary of all 16 tests, followed by the complete name list and the common family template.

---

## Common idiom (used verbatim in every file — the load-bearing snippet)

```c
static inline uint64x2_t load_vec(const void *addr) {
    uint64x2_t res;
    __asm__ volatile ("ldr %q0, [%1]" : "=w"(res) : "r"(addr) : "memory");
    return res;
}
static inline void store_vec(void *addr, uint64x2_t val) { vst1q_u64((uint64_t*)addr, val); }
```
The `asm volatile` + `"memory"` clobber is what keeps the **dead** loads/stores from being DCE'd or reordered — it forces a literal `ldr q, [xN]` (plain base addressing, no offset/writeback). Any SVE port must preserve "real, unschedulable-away ldr at top" semantics.

Common to all 16 DECLARE_TESTs: `.quality_level = TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **no** `.groups`, **no** `.flags`, **no** `.test_preinit`, **no** `.minimum_cpu` gate. All are pure aarch64 (only the helpers are `#if defined(__aarch64__)`-guarded; the data structs use NEON types unconditionally, so the files cannot compile on x86 — they must be meson-gated per-arch). All include `sandstone.h` + `<arm_neon.h>` (guarded).

Two lineages inside the family (critical for ports):
- **Original-parent lineage** (`neon_rot_ldr_at_top`, 2026-09-08): plain forward `for (i = 0; i < COUNT; i++)` sweep. Members: sub, mla, offdiag.
- **Rowmajor-parent lineage** (`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor`): alternating sweep direction —
  ```c
  const bool ascending = (sweep & 1) == 0;
  const int i = ascending ? n : (COUNT - 1 - n);
  ```
  Members: str3, ldr4, rowmajor_dump, gps, dualcmp, str3_checkall, k5far, k5inter_rand, k3res, k7p×4.

## 7. `/…/neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_gps.cpp`

- **test name**: `neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_gps` — desc: "GPS-tagged chassis of ldr_at_top_rowmajor: every 64b word self-reports its source (magic|byte_off|~byte_off|gen); Phase 0' B-track of the readpath-localization campaign". PROD.
- **lifecycle**: init `mkdir("movbe_log/gps_rowmajor", 0755)`; **tagged fill replaces memset_random** — the only functional delta. Golden computed from tagged data with the parent rotation (tags flow through the ALU; e.g. eor words carry magic A^B = 0xFFFF in the top half).
- **memory**: standard 4×16 KiB; no fd (per-fail files instead).
- **core loop**: byte-identical to rowmajor parent (objdump-verified per header); hot loop never branches on tags.
- **verification**: per-sweep memcmp(dst); on mismatch, cold path writes the **five-buffer snapshot** (dst, expected, srcA, srcB, scratch, in that order) + trailing text line `cpu=%d sweep=%lu` to `movbe_log/gps_rowmajor/fail_cpu<cpu>_sweep<sweep>.bin`, then `report_fail_msg`. Classification is fully **offline** (wrong-line / wrong-word / misaligned window / two-source splice / ALU-mix-in / bitflip / unknown).
- **RNG**: none — deterministic GPS tags (generation held constant 0 on purpose; rotating it would dirty srcA/srcB lines and break the init golden).
- **special**: tag layout per 64-bit word: bits 63..48 magic (srcA=0xA5A5, srcB=0x5A5A, scratch=0x0F0F), 47..32 byte_off, 31..16 ~byte_off (integrity check), 15..0 generation=0. Fill idiom:
  ```c
  store_vec(&data->srcA[i], vcombine_u64(vcreate_u64(gps_tag(MAGIC_A, byte+0, 0)),
                                         vcreate_u64(gps_tag(MAGIC_A, byte+8, 0))));  /* byte = i*16 */
  ```
  A/B magics complementary so a two-source splice is visible inside one word. Dump dir is **relative** (CWD-dependent). Header: "no LCG seed fixing; auto-seed only" (moot — no RNG used).
- **delta**: fill-only change (structured tags instead of random) + five-buffer dump; hot loop untouched. Turns captured fails into self-describing evidence of *where each byte came from*.

## 8. `/…/neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_dualcmp.cpp`

- **test name**: `neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_dualcmp` — desc: "Dual-store comparison: baseline skeleton, checks BOTH str targets (temp & dst) + their mutual consistency — which store leg carries the SDC, or is it upstream of the fork". PROD.
- **lifecycle**: standard init + `mkdir` of the same `movbe_log/gps_rowmajor` dir.
- **memory**: standard 4×16 KiB shared; per-thread temp/dst.
- **core loop**: byte-identical to rowmajor baseline (2 stores: temp then dst).
- **verification** — the whole point: **two unconditional memcmps per sweep** (dst vs golden, temp vs golden); if either fails, `dualcmp_classify()` (cold) walks all indices using `vceqq_u64` + `temp[i][0] == dst[i][0]` (GCC vector-subscript extension) and fills `DualCmpStats { a_only, b_only, ab_div, ab_same, first_bad }`:
  - a_only = dst wrong, temp right → 2nd store leg;
  - b_only = temp wrong, dst right → 1st store leg;
  - ab_div = temp != dst (stores diverged; defect at/after the fork);
  - ab_same = temp == dst != golden (upstream of the fork: load/ALU/bypass).
  Dumps dst, expected, temp, srcA, srcB + stats line to `dualcmp_fail_cpu<cpu>_sweep<sweep>.bin`; `report_fail_msg` with the counter summary.
- **RNG**: memset_random; "No LCG seed fixing; auto seed only."
- **special**: within-run A/B leg comparison immune to layout confound (both stores share one loop/sweep/timing); pre-registered readouts in header.
- **delta**: only the cold path grows — the family never before checked `temp` (the 1st store target). Converts the double-store idiom from a timing trick into a measurement of which store leg corrupts.

## 13–16. `/…/neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_k7pattern.cpp` (4 tests, one shared implementation)

Shared `k7p_init_common(test, pattern)` / `k7p_run_common(test, cpu, name)` / `k7p_cleanup_common`; the four DECLARE_TESTs differ only in the fill pattern enum and the name string used in dump filenames and fail messages. All PROD; all standard 4×16 KiB buffers, rowmajor skeleton (dead scratch ldr at top, srcA/srcB, add/eor/and/orr by i%4, str/str), per-sweep memcmp(dst) + five-buffer dump to `movbe_log/gps_rowmajor/<name>_fail_cpu<cpu>_sweep<sweep>.bin` + `report_fail_msg("%s data miscompare", name)`.

Fill via `pattern_word(p, which, byte_off)` (`which`: 0=srcA, 1=srcB, 2=scratch):

- **`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_k7p_zero`** — "K7 pattern cell: all-zero operands (activation floor of the 2x64b path)". Every word 0x0000000000000000; with constant operands the golden is the constant expectation, so any corruption is trivially visible. Activation floor.
- **`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_k7p_one`** — "K7 pattern cell: all-one operands (complementary activation floor)". Every word 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. Complementary floor.
- **`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_k7p_rand`** — "K7 pattern cell: GPS-tagged random operands (B-track baseline; doubles as dump-capable A-track for Phase 0.5)". GPS tags identical to the gps chassis (magic/byte_off/~byte_off/gen structure) so the field-substitution classifier works on it.
- **`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor_k7p_hiham`** — "K7 pattern cell: 0x55/0xAA alternating high-Hamming operands (maximum transition density)". Per-byte: `nib = ((byte_off + b) & 1) ? 0xAA : 0x55` — every adjacent byte pair differs in 8 bits, and byte_off parity is recoverable offline.

- **RNG**: none of the four uses memset_random; all fills deterministic (rand cell uses the deterministic GPS-tag generator, not RNG — despite the name).
- **special**: battery purpose — separate pattern-activation from physical-lane effects (parent lane curve: 2×64b = 223 fails/30 min, 4×32b = 0, 16×8b = 2; op bias orr 71% / and 23% / eor 5% / add 1%, damage avoids all-0/all-1 segments). Pre-registered: zero/one ~0 while rand/hiham fail → pattern gating; all similar → lane shape; hiham >> rand → transition density matters.
- **delta (file vs siblings)**: the only multi-test file; four cells of a fill-only axis sharing one code path; note the *name-vs-behaviour* quirk that k7p_rand is GPS-tagged (deterministic), not memset_random.

## Common family template

**Loop skeleton** (all 16; "hot loop", identical shape modulo the stated deltas):

```c
TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13) {                       /* outer timed loop, ≤8192 sweeps */
    /* rowmajor lineage only: */
    const bool ascending = (sweep & 1) == 0;
    for (int n = 0; n < COUNT; n++) {
        const int i = ascending ? n : (COUNT - 1 - n);   /* original lineage: i = n */
        uint64x2_t unused_x = load_vec(&data->scratch[i]); (void)unused_x;  /* DEAD ldr AT TOP */
        uint64x2_t a = load_vec(&data->srcA[i]);          /* useful load 1 */
        uint64x2_t b = load_vec(&data->srcB[i]);          /* useful load 2 */
        switch (i % 4) { /* 0:add 1:eor 2:and 3:orr  — rotating ALU, per-index op mix */ }
```

## Common idiom (used verbatim in every file — the load-bearing snippet)

```c
static inline uint64x2_t load_vec(const void *addr) {
    uint64x2_t res;
    __asm__ volatile ("ldr %q0, [%1]" : "=w"(res) : "r"(addr) : "memory");
    return res;
}
static inline void store_vec(void *addr, uint64x2_t val) { vst1q_u64((uint64_t*)addr, val); }
```
The `asm volatile` + `"memory"` clobber is what keeps the **dead** loads/stores from being DCE'd or reordered — it forces a literal `ldr q, [xN]` (plain base addressing, no offset/writeback). Any SVE port must preserve "real, unschedulable-away ldr at top" semantics.

Common to all 16 DECLARE_TESTs: `.quality_level = TEST_QUALITY_PROD`; **no** `.groups`, **no** `.flags`, **no** `.test_preinit`, **no** `.minimum_cpu` gate. All are pure aarch64 (only the helpers are `#if defined(__aarch64__)`-guarded; the data structs use NEON types unconditionally, so the files cannot compile on x86 — they must be meson-gated per-arch). All include `sandstone.h` + `<arm_neon.h>` (guarded).

Two lineages inside the family (critical for ports):
- **Original-parent lineage** (`neon_rot_ldr_at_top`, 2026-09-08): plain forward `for (i = 0; i < COUNT; i++)` sweep. Members: sub, mla, offdiag.
- **Rowmajor-parent lineage** (`neon_rot_ldr_at_top_rowmajor`): alternating sweep direction —
  ```c
  const bool ascending = (sweep & 1) == 0;
  const int i = ascending ? n : (COUNT - 1 - n);
  ```
  Members: str3, ldr4, rowmajor_dump, gps, dualcmp, str3_checkall, k5far, k5inter_rand, k3res, k7p×4.

---

## 1. `/…/neon_rot_ldr_at_top_sub.cpp`

- **test name**: `neon_rot_ldr_at_top_sub` — desc: "ALU-dimension variant of ldr_at_top: rotation sub/eor/bic/orn (carry vs combinational signature test)". PROD, no groups/flags.

## Common family template

**Loop skeleton** (all 16; "hot loop", identical shape modulo the stated deltas):

```c
TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13) {                       /* outer timed loop, ≤8192 sweeps */
    /* rowmajor lineage only: */
    const bool ascending = (sweep & 1) == 0;
    for (int n = 0; n < COUNT; n++) {
        const int i = ascending ? n : (COUNT - 1 - n);   /* original lineage: i = n */
        uint64x2_t unused_x = load_vec(&data->scratch[i]); (void)unused_x;  /* DEAD ldr AT TOP */
        uint64x2_t a = load_vec(&data->srcA[i]);          /* useful load 1 */
        uint64x2_t b = load_vec(&data->srcB[i]);          /* useful load 2 */
        switch (i % 4) { /* 0:add 1:eor 2:and 3:orr  — rotating ALU, per-index op mix */ }
        store_vec(&temp[i], res);                          /* back-to-back stores */
        store_vec(&dst[i],  res);                          /* (str3 family: + junk[i]) */
    }
    sweep++;
    if (memcmp(dst, data->expected, COUNT * sizeof(uint64x2_t)) != 0)   /* COLD path */
        report_fail_msg("… data miscompare");
}
```
The probed hardware behavior: a load/store-unit defect on the failing core such that, under this exact micro-op mix — dead load(s) placed *before* the two source loads, 2-source vector ALU, back-to-back stores of one result — stored results occasionally contain wrong bits (measured signature: same-buffer field substitution from a neighbouring word, ±8..±28 elements away, op-biased toward orr/and). The `asm volatile` ldr is non-removable and keeps its position; `vst1q` stores are also not DCE-able because dst is memcmp'd (and temp is dead-but-kept via the volatile-store path only where checked).

**Buffer layout**: COUNT = 1024 elements × 16 B = 16 KiB per buffer (k3res: 4096/64 KiB; k5far/k5inter_rand: interleaved src = 2048 elements/32 KiB; offdiag: interleaved = 3072/48 KiB), all `aligned_alloc(64, …)`. Shared (allocated in `test_init`, child main thread, before per-CPU workers spawn; written only during init, read-only afterwards — race-free by construction): srcA/srcB/scratch(/scratch2)/interleaved-src + expected (golden). Per-thread (allocated inside `test_run`, freed at its end): temp, dst (+ junk in str3 family). This matches the shared-vs-per-thread discipline the sdcshield fork fixed in 1023c841 — keep it in the SVE ports.

**Init golden rule**: expected[i] is precomputed in init with the *same intrinsics, same operand order, same NEON units* as the hot loop, so any runtime mismatch is hardware, not compiler drift. Fill is either `memset_random` (auto-seeded framework RNG, per-run) or a deterministic GPS-tag/pattern fill; deterministic fills replace RNG entirely.

**Cold-path menu** (compose per variant): plain memcmp(dst) → fail (sub, mla, offdiag, str3, ldr4); + per-index log/bin records with cold source re-read (rowmajor_dump, str3_checkall); + five-buffer file dump to `movbe_log/gps_rowmajor/` (gps, dualcmp, k5far, k5inter_rand, k3res, k7p×4); multi-target checks: dualcmp (temp+dst+mutual), str3_checkall (temp+junk+dst slot_mask).

**Porting notes**: no knobs, no `log_skip`, no preinit, no `minimum_cpu`; `TEST_LOOP(test, 1<<13)` fixed; `device_info[cpu].cpu_number` used to map the `cpu` thread parameter to logical CPU in dump records; `dualcmp_classify` uses the GCC `uint64x2_t::operator[]` vector extension; dump dirs `movbe_log/gps_rowmajor` are CWD-relative while `/var/tmp/…_<pid>.bin` is absolute; shared dump fds are appended from all worker threads (single `write()` per record).

All in `/home/sdc/root-xupeng/sdcshield/missing_testcases_20261009/tests/cpu/arm-0102/`. **None of the 4 exist anywhere in the repo build tree** (repo's `tests/cpu/arm-0102/` contains only `arm0102_kreg_mask.cpp`, registered at `tests/cpu/meson.build:261` in `tests_set_base`).

## Shared template (identical across all 4 — the "verified core-179 trigger recipe")

- **Declaration**: `DECLARE_TEST(name, "desc")` with `.test_init`, `.test_run`, `.test_cleanup`, `.quality_level = TEST_QUALITY_PROD`. **No `.groups`, no `.flags`, no `.minimum_cpu`, no `.fracture_loop_count`** (contrast: the eigen tests use `group_math` + `fracture_loop_count=5`).
- **Init** (runs once, child main thread): `malloc` a struct + `aligned_alloc(64, ...)` persistent heap source buffers (COUNT=1024 vector elements = 16 KB each) + an `expected` buffer; sources filled with `memset_random` (framework per-thread RNG); **golden precomputed in init with the exact same NEON ops and same `i % 4` rotation** — self-consistent golden on the same NEON units.
- **Run** (per-CPU worker thread): allocates **per-thread** `temp` + `dst` buffers; `TEST_LOOP(test, 1 << 13)`; inner sweep over 1024 elements:
  - 2 (or 3) source loads via inline asm — `__asm__ volatile ("ldr %q0, [%1]" : "=w"(res) : "r"(addr) : "memory")` — asm boundary is REQUIRED (comment: the compiler eliminates intrinsic reloads, so the guaranteed `ldr q` would not appear in the binary);
  - payload op rotated across 4 variants per `i % 4` (alu-instruction rotation "REQUIRED" per the recipe);
  - amplifier: `store_vec(&temp[i], res); store_vec(&dst[i], load_vec(&temp[i]));` — guaranteed back-to-back str q → ldr q → str q;
  - cold-path check after each sweep: `memcmp(dst, data->expected, 16KB)` → `report_fail_msg` on mismatch.
- **Race risk: none.** `test->data` (srcA/srcB/expected) is shared across worker threads but strictly **read-only** during run; `temp`/`dst` are per-thread heap allocations. (This is the correct pattern — unlike the fixed `insert_extract_sve` shared-buffer race.) Golden is computed once in init before workers spawn.
- **RNG**: framework `memset_random` only; fma_f32 additionally re-rolls lanes via `frandomf_scale(100.0f)` (raw random bits can be NaN/Inf).
- **Portability note**: the data struct uses `uint32x4_t` members **outside** the `#if defined(__aarch64__)` guard, so these files are aarch64-only source and must be meson-gated (as `arm0102_kreg_mask.cpp` is).

## Per-file specifics

| File | Test name | Origin | Payload rotation (i%4) | NEON intrinsics |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `arm0102_kreg_select.cpp` | `arm0102_kreg_select` | `tests/cpu/vector/kreg1.cpp` vbslq branch | bsl `vbslq_u32(a,b,b^a)` / bit `vbslq_u32(a,a,b)` / bif `vbslq_u32(a,b,a)` / mixed `vbslq_u32(a, and(a,b), eor(a,b))` | `vbslq_u32`, `vandq_u32`, `veorq_u32` (uint32x4_t) |
| `arm0102_kreg_not.cpp` | `arm0102_kreg_not` | `kreg4.cpp` (mvn semantics) | nand `vmvnq(vandq)` / nor `vmvnq(vorrq)` / xnor `vmvnq(veorq)` / nandnot `vmvnq(vbicq)` | `vmvnq_u32` (bitwise NOT), `vandq/vorrq/veorq/vbicq_u32` |
| `arm0102_kreg_logic.cpp` | `arm0102_kreg_logic` | `kreg1.cpp` mask logic | and / or / xor / andnot | `vandq_u32`, `vorrq_u32`, `veorq_u32`, `vbicq_u32` |
| `arm0102_fma_f32.cpp` | `arm0102_fma_f32` | `tests/cpu/fma/fma.cpp` | fma `vfmaq(c,a,b)` / fms `vfmsq` / fnma `vneg(vfmsq(vneg(c),a,b))` / fnms `vneg(vfmaq(vneg(c),a,b))` | `vfmaq_f32`, `vfmsq_f32`, `vnegq_f32` (float32x4_t; **3** source loads — a, b, and addend c) |

**On the "kreg" question**: x86 kreg = AVX-512 mask registers; these ARM variants emulate mask ops with NEON **32-bit-lane** bitwise select/NOT/logic on full 128-bit vectors. **No 8/16-bit lane ops appear anywhere** (no `vbslq_u8/u16`, no narrowing). The only byte-lane-adjacent member of this family is the repo's already-ported `arm0102_kreg_mask.cpp` (compare-mask expansion via `vceqq/vcgtq/vtstq_u32` — still 32-bit lanes).

## Existing SVE porting precedents (directly reusable)

# PART 2 — The eigen files

## `svd_cdouble_noavx512.cpp` (missing_testcases copy)

**Byte-identical to the repo's own `/home/sdc/root-xupeng/sdcshield/tests/cpu/eigen_svd/svd_cdouble_noavx512.cpp`** (`diff` rc=0) — the repo already has and builds this test (in `tests_set_base`, `tests/cpu/meson.build:374`).

- Operational caveat: the runtime-VL rule — `tests_sve` compiles at `-msve-vector-bits=128` while the host is VL=256, so running `eigen_svd_cdouble_sve` standalone on this machine requires pinning the task VL (`prctl` launcher in `scripts/eigen-sve-double/`).
